Float Around: This Inflatable Tent Is for Land and Sea and Can Fit Four People Inside Overnight
24 photos
Photo: Sonmez Outdoor
If you’re camping with the buddies near a lake, God forbid you be the last one to wake up in the morning. If you are, you could very well do so while floating in the middle of said lake on your air mattress; we all know that prank. However, one team decided to make some serious bank with a product that embraces the spirit of the prank and really runs with it.
It’s called the Floating Tent and tells you all you really need to know about what the heck it can do and why it's so special. While we’ve shed light upon this design before, a few years back, this thing is so neat and works like a charm that in all the time it's been on the market, it’s gone unchanged.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family Back when the floating tent first hit the scene, it was considered the first in the world, crafted by a team dubbed Sonmez Outdoor, a brand that saw its beginning in Turkey, and these days, sells these babies worldwide. They do have a US-based website for potential North American buyers, so if you fall in love with this solution by the end of the article, you can easily get your hands on one.
Keep in mind that Sonmez isn’t just some random team that spits out a product that has me thinking twice about spending the night in it, but rather, has been in the business of making tents for years, be they classic options with poles for support or inflatable tents that make setup a breeze.
The Floating Tent belongs to the latter category and does require a pump to be used in order to give it its final shape. Once we do, we have access to a four-person tent that places 43 square feet (4 square meters) of usable floorspace at our disposal.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family Yet, those 43 square feet aren’t just to be used for a couple of sleeping bags - they can - but it's the ability to do whatever you want with the interior, including laying down a dining table, bringing in a portable power bank, or whatever your plans entail. Some folks are clearly bringing along fishing gear and bait for some very calming overnight fishing.
Think about that for a second: the Floating Tent goes well beyond the average experience that a two-person boat with an outboard motor can offer, in that you can just float out onto the water, fish, cook what you catch if you have the necessary gear, and then, with a full belly, just pass out. Don’t forget to pull down the insect nets because mosquitos out on the water are just something else ; good luck sleeping if you forget.
As for what you’ll be sleeping on - if you don’t wish to bring along a sleeping bag or anything of the like - is a PVC floor, marine-grade PVC, to be precise, and according to the manufacturer, it’s fireproof and antibacterial, not to mention 100% waterproof.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family The inflatable columns and outer rim of the floor are also PVC, and on top of it all sits a layer of polyester fabric with a 100% waterproof rating. Even if you’re caught out there in a storm, you’ll wake up after it’s passed with everything as dry as, something to do with nuns... you probably know some variation of the proverb. It can handle 80 kph (50 mph) winds.
An acrylic coating is in place too, further protecting the tent, but it’s not clear where that coating is found. Based on my knowledge of how inflatable tents are made, I'd say that this coating is found on the exterior of the PVC, to help strengthen the tubes.
What I found rather wild is that the manufacturer’s website mentions that this one is good for use in all four seasons, which I'd say is a bit of a stretch considering there is no heating system inside, but you could very well grab a heating solution and try your luck.
Who knows, maybe this thing is so impermeable that your own body heat can make the interior toasty. If that’s true, you’ll need to worry about condensation forming and dripping down on your dry goods.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family In terms of installation, Sonmez mentions that it can take as little as five minutes for this odd-ball glamping solution to be ready to carry you out in the middle of nowhere with your significant other. Bring food and drinks, not to mention a blanket and some mosquito repellant, just in case one makes it inside.
What you need to finally consider is that the Floating Tent weighs 110 lbs (50 kg), so you’ll need some help to move it around and set up, unless you hit the gym regularly, and secondly, this thing has no actual motor anywhere.
So, you’ll either need to give it one very big push, live at the whim of the lake for the next day or night, and then call a buddy to come out with a dinghy to push or tow you back to shore, or just grab two paddles and work your way back when you’re ready; you’ll have to work as a team with your significant other or friends.
Photo: Sonmez Outdoor Then again, there are some low-power trolly motors out there that have been developed for fishing and just work with that. Lightweight electric options exist too, so don’t worry about overloading your floating haven; there’s no mention of how much it can handle.
Keep in mind that since the Floating Tent hit the scene, there have been countless folks that said “yes” and gave it a try, and the general consensus is that this one is a hit, especially since it can be used on both “sea” and land.
But, it isn’t perfect, and as I foretold, there are mentions that condensation can be an issue, not to mention the actual anchoring so that you don’t go off drifting with the motion of the ocean, so to speak.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family Last but not least, price is a big factor that people complain about. At a selling price of $4,600, it is by no means cheap, and it is because of this factor that some folks have simply said “pass.”. Nonetheless, those that have stepped up to the plate, have actually found it a neat little gimmick to tap into: being able to float around on a lake in a tent.
Personally, I can see so many uses for this thing, including a neat little summer rental service out on a nearby lake. I’ll just take you out to wherever it is you want to float, anchor the tent down, and come back to pick you up in the morning.
How much would you be willing to spend for a night on the lake with the Mr. or Mrs.? I’d be open to drop $50 to $100 on the experience. Would you? Leave your thoughts below because I'm very curious if I need to start a side hustle next summer.
